Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old male with 3-day history of diarrhea, central abdominal pain, and one episode of vomiting; likely acute gastroenteritis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days.
- Timeline: Onset 3 days ago; neither improving nor worsening.
- Associated symptoms: Central abdominal pain (below belly button), described as relieved somewhat after defecation or passing gas; one episode of vomiting in the morning; occasional nausea.
- Vomitus: No blood (initial concern but clarified to be from strawberries consumed).
- Diarrhea: Frequent urgency; stool frequency enough to interfere with work; feeling of incomplete evacuation.
- Fluid intake: Patient unsure, suspects possibly not enough water.
- Appetite: Eating less due to frequent stools; had fruit for breakfast, vomited afterwards.
- Blood in stool: Denied.
- Other symptoms: Denies chest pain, no new or worsening breathing problems beyond baseline asthma, no walking/talking limitation due to cardiorespiratory symptom (limited by need for toilet access).
- Recent fever: Denies any significant fever; had some sweating over the last four days but not sure if febrile.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Pain somewhat alleviated by going to the toilet.
- Systems review: Denies chest pain, new shortness of breath, or blood in vomit/stool.
- No mention of sick contacts or dietary indiscretion, but patient concerned about role of new inhaler.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma; uses inhaler (specific medication, dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: NKDA (No known drug allergies).

Social History:
- Work: Unable to go to work due to diarrhea.
- No mention of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.
- Foreigner; mentioned changing inhaler brand after moving.

Family History:
- Father died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.

Physical Examination:
- No examination or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or mentioned.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis (likely)
  - Drink plenty of fluids.
  - Monitor for fever or worsening symptoms.
  - Remain at home until symptoms improve.
  - Antibiotics not indicated (may worsen condition).
  - Seek in-person GP review if symptoms worsen or persist.
- Issue 2: Asthma (well controlled, no acute exacerbation)
  - Continue inhaler as usual.
- Issue 3: Family history of bowel cancer
  - Less likely to be cause of current acute symptoms given clinical picture.
  - If symptoms persist beyond acute illness, evaluation by GP may be warranted.

General plan items:
- Patient advised to monitor for new red flag symptoms (bleeding, persistent vomiting, increased pain, fever).
- Follow up with GP if worsening or not improving in the next few days.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing elements:
  - No medication reconciliation beyond inhaler.
  - Allergies documented, but medications (type of inhaler, dose, frequency) not specified.
  - No physical examination or vital signs performed.
  - No stool description, travel, sick contact, or risk factor history.
  - No social, alcohol, or tobacco use history.
● No internal conflicts noted; minor initial uncertainty about blood in vomitus, clarified as not blood.
● Transcript quality: Some conversational interruptions and minor confusion, but clinically relevant information extractable.
